newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks remain mixed on China policy.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks remain mixed on China policy.

text.p: Taiwan share prices remained mixed in late Friday trade despite the island's top economic policymaker telling local businessmen it was time to slow investments in mainland China, brokers said.
"It is time to slow our investment in the mainland," Chiang Ping-kun, chairman of the cabinet's Council for Economic Planning and Development told Reuters.
With 50 minutes left, the index was up 0.71 points or 0.01 percent at 6,426.39 on a modest turnover of T$23.7 billion.
But China-concept shares fell on Chiang's remarks, with President Enterprises down 60 cents T$41.2.
Construction and cement scrips rose, but food and rubber shares fell.
"The market did not react much to chairman Chiang's remarks as this was well expected, and rising foreign fund inflows since August helped support sentiment," said Amy Huang of Nomura Securities.
She expected consolidation to continue for some time as the market was also waiting for development in the Gulf.
